page: Microsoft Azure E64as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores across an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and hardware AES encryption. Memory provisioning is substantial, featuring 512.0 GB of RAM with an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, designed specifically for footprint-heavy computational environments. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached remote block storage for persistence.

Performance evaluation demonstrates high parallel processing capabilities across demanding computational tasks. The instance records a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21,907 alongside top-tier image processing metrics and a strong PassMark CPU score of 75,983.61. Multi-threaded decompression reaches 375.99 GB/sec in bzip3 tests, complemented by cached memory read throughput of 4,863.52 GB/sec. Memory-intensive operational loads register 88.78 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and strong database throughput scores. LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier prompt processing throughput on small 135M parameter models at 4,447.51 tokens per second, while larger models see moderate throughput governed by CPU execution constraints.

Qualitatively, the E64as_v6 presents an efficient resource balance for architectures requiring extensive physical memory capacity without requiring dedicated accelerators. Because local storage is absent, architects must factor in external storage provisioning overhead and bandwidth limits for I/O paths. The platform fits enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching clusters, high-concurrency static web serving, memory-resident ETL pipelines, and continuous integration compilation jobs requiring substantial RAM buffers.

The instance includes no onboard local storage and no GPU hardware, utilizing external network volumes for persistence.
